findings.suggested_fix: In the finish === 'Skip' branch, assert data-attack-state=idle and black turn immediately after the 32 ms runFor, before the common 5000 ms advance. In fireworm_refinement.spec.js:82, advance only 32 ms after tap, assert idle and black turn, then retain the 4000 ms stale-timeline advance and assertions. Rerun these Skip cases on desktop and phone portrait/landscape.
findings.title: Assert Fireworm Skip before natural completion can mask failure
findings.why_it_matters: The Fireworm touch-Skip cases can pass even when the tap does not skip the capture. The clock is paused, but the test advances 5000 ms after the tap before checking idle and the committed turn, which exceeds the entire 3350 ms Fireworm animation. A broken or unreachable Skip therefore falls through to natural completion and satisfies every subsequent check. The moved-Flamehuffer refinement test has the same issue with its 4000 ms advance at line 82. As the generic production browser Skip tests already do, assert idle and the committed turn after one input frame, then advance beyond the abandoned timeline to check that no stale completion occurs.
findings.validation_reason: If the Fireworm canvas Skip tap is missed or broken, the paused-clock tests still advance 5000 ms (e2e/fireworm.spec.js:54) or 4000 ms (e2e/fireworm_refinement.spec.js:82), exceeding the 3350 ms natural finish at FirewormPresenter.ts:121 before checking the committed turn; both tests are newly introduced by this diff, and helpers add no immediate Skip assertion, so the gap is established from code while actual missed-Skip incidence was not measured.
